theme_note: These passages all make the room's own April Fools day into joint play: people post character jokes, deliberately disobey a no-upvote instruction, coin mashup names, and tease a duplicate post. The images and the ways commenters extend them vary; the shared practice is playing along with the local joke, not doing anything on the canvas.

second_order: getting the Planeptune N onto the canvas
theme_note: These passages turn a broad wish for Gamindustri to appear into the modest N that participants say they finished. They vary from choosing a mark, place, sprite, and size to reporting completion and celebrating that it exists.

second_order: building, fixing, and watching the pixels together
theme_note: These passages coordinate the hands-on upkeep of shared work. What varies is the job—outlining, choosing a blue, fixing a ring, guarding, giving placement instructions, or handing the mark to the next person—but each tells people how to make or tend pixels together.

second_order: trying more pictures without wiping out neighbours
theme_note: These passages seek representation beyond the small N while treating other people's work as a limit. The desired additions vary—Purple Heart, other CPUs, or any Nep picture—and so do the constraints, but the common practice is trying to expand without purging or crowding neighbours.

second_order: cheering and thanking the people who made it
theme_note: These passages affirm the shared effort and its contributors. The form varies from calling the project fun and applauding a valuable helper to later thanks, congratulations, drinks, pudding, and character-voiced praise.

second_order: catching latecomers up on what people had done
theme_note: These passages orient someone who arrives without the current account: they answer a late proposal by saying the logo already exists and later explain the event or the earlier logo episode. What varies is whether the catch-up concerns accomplishment, rules, or a reference.

second_order: keeping r/place from taking over the room
theme_note: These passages set limits on how canvas conflict spills into subreddit talk. One contrasts this room with another subreddit flooded by r/place; another stops a football argument. The situations differ, but both contain the event's takeover of ordinary discussion.

second_order: looking outside the thread for coordination and permission
theme_note: These passages reach beyond the visible thread to coordinate or secure room to build. The practice develops from asking another subreddit and suggesting a Discord into applications, spreadsheets, Discord negotiation, and returned proof; what varies is whether the outward move is proposed, performed, or reported back.

second_order: defending the Nep as a war
theme_note: These passages mobilize people to hold or restore the Planeptune mark by casting pixel work as invasion, faith, duty, red alert, battle, and victory. They vary between urgent calls, concrete tactical choices, vigilance, character-voiced devotion, and an adapted call-and-answer speech; what holds them together is using war play to sustain defense.

These passages make the second CPU logo: they call for builders, notice construction, adjust its border and location, specify the black-and-blue design, and report completion. The stages vary, but all advance Lastation as the concrete second mark.

These passages reciprocate or protect nearby groups: participants propose helping GreenLattice for room, clean an area to earn goodwill, preserve Zoro, recount defending neighbouring works, and welcome a neighbour. The neighbours and form of help vary; the practice is treating assistance as mutual rather than merely avoiding conflict.

second_order: retelling the pixel work as the Grand Battle
theme_note: These passages turn the finished or recorded work into a shared account: inviting witnesses, narrating defense and expansion, naming a Grand Battle or Great War, spotting allies in the record, and recounting alliances. The medium and emphasis vary, but each makes a story of what participants say happened.

second_order: showing people where the finished logos are
theme_note: These passages help people find or view the completed work through positions, landmarks, links, and screenshots. What varies is who asks and which aid answers; the common practice is making the canvas result visible to someone who cannot locate it.

second_order: rebuilding on placeTwo after r/place ended
theme_note: These passages carry the symbol-making into the named successor canvas after the original closes. They vary from adding Planeptune and Lastation to reporting loss and proposing Lowee, Leanbox, or Purple Heart, but all continue building on placeTwo rather than on the finished event canvas.

second_order: settling scores with r/49ers after the end
theme_note: These passages look back at r/49ers as the defeated antagonist: participants condemn displacement, laugh at insults or blemishes, contrast anime and football fans, caricature the attack, and repeat that they won. The moral criticism, ridicule, and triumph vary; the common practice is post-event score-settling.
